a.text: The rumble of the Originium boilers has yet to cease. Thick plumes of smog gush out of the towering chimneys.
The workmen take off their worn-out protective gear and hand it off to the next shift.
The day is nearing its end here in Caladon.

steps.text: November 16th, 1097, 9:50 P.M.
Nine in the evening is when the Infected factory nearby changes shifts.
Many of the workmen choose to kill time by paying Miss Quercus's shop a visit.
There is not much the shop has to offer to its patrons.
A crude fried fin cutlet, a bowl of tasteless potato soup, and a mug of fruit-wine-flavored water.
And yet, the shop has garnered a few regulars.

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: Cheers!

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: Cheers!

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: Hahahaha! Here's to Brande!

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: Hey, Sparky! Another pint!

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Here you go. Your fruit wine.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: So what's going on? Why's everybody so cheery?

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: Mr. Brande just gave us all a bonus along with our payslips for the month!

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: They say it's a bonus, but it's just a hundred pence.

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: And considering they work us to the bone, that's the least they could owe us.

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: You sure you should be here at this hour, though? Might get a beating from the missus?

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: Jog on! I'm the king of the castle! She wouldn't dare!

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: Alright. Here's to the king of the castle!

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: Cheers!

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: Hey, Sparky! Another pint!

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Hahaha... Mr. James, you really should watch your drink, though. We wouldn't want to upset Mrs. James.

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: Sparky, I heard from your boss you've got something stronger than this piss?

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: Get us some of that!

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Not! Happening!

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Remember what Miss Quercus told you. Strong drink is bad for your condition!

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: You need to take better care of yourself, Stone.

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: Come on, what's the problem?

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: This disease is a death sentence. Might as well get a taste of the hard stuff before we cark...

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Don't say that!

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: The doctors in the city told us! Oripathy progresses differently depending on the patient's physical condition!

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: Lighten up, I'm just...

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Stone!

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: Um... Yeah?

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Take care of yourself and live life to the fullest! Stop saying that word all the time!

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: Er... Sorry?

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: Look at you. You got Sparky upset.

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: *Sigh*, I didn't mean to...

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: Huh? Looks like we've got quite a crowd here today.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Good evening, Mr. Root!

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: Oi, if it isn't Bitter Root! Come on, come on! Let's drink!

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: Huh? Something to celebrate today?
Caladon's Infected community is home to many a peculiar man, and Bitter Root counts among them.
Mr. Root works for an organization called Rhodes Island. He's a 'professional' hired by the lords of the city council.
But the way Rhodes Island treats the Infected boggles the mind.
'Rhodes Island will assist the Caladon City Council and provide medical assistance to all Infected,' said their public address.
Why would anyone willingly help the Infected... especially when they're not even from here?

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: How's work today, Bitt? T'ain't often you get the free time to come for a drink.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: It's fine. We hired a few extra pair of hands. Things calmed down quite a bit, thanks to them.

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: Eh? Is it that good working for Rhodes Island? Do they pay well?

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: What of it? You interested?

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: Nah, forget I said anything. I can't even read... I'd just be making a fool of myself.
At first, no one in the Infected community trusted them. There were even rumors that they were here to take the late-stage Infected away for experiments.
But Rhodes Island proved themselves with their actions. They really are here to help.
Be it a regular Oripathy infection checkup, acute Oripathy attack treatment, or even just a normal workplace injury, you just walk into their clinic, and they'll help you.
Even right here, right now, there are those who have doubts about Rhodes Island's true motives. But at the very least, all of the pub's regulars trust them.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: By the way, Jim, I saw your wife on my way here.

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: What? What?? You sure?! Oh, bugger...

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: Ahem.

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: Er... You carry on with the drinks. I... I just remembered I've got a few errands to run. See you around!

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: Hahaha, there goes our 'king of the castle!'

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: Yeah, yeah, off I go. We'll do this another time.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Be safe on your way home, Mr. James.
Unlike most of the people in the establishment, Mr. James is not Infected.
In Caladon, it isn't uncommon to find non-Infected working in the Infected community.
Ever since the 'New Caladon Infected Act' came into place, a lot of the unemployed poor have been risking themselves working in the Infected factories.
A great majority of them leave the Infected community as soon as they get off work. They also avoid coming into direct contact with the Infected during working hours.
That's understandable. All of us Infected have gotten used to the attitude, and no one blames the non-Infected workmen for it.
Though, still, there are people like Mr. James.

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: *Sigh*. There goes my drinking buddy.

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: Come on, Bean, stop spacing out over there. Have a few pints with me.

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: Quiet down. I'm reading the newspaper.

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: What's the headlines?

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: It's all been big news the last couple of days! The whole town's talking about it. Don't tell me you haven't heard!

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: The new bill, is it? That's some big news, indeed.

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: What new bill?

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: The one that's going to improve how us Infected workers are treated! Do you ever do anything except drink? This bill's going to be massive for all of us!

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: Peh, and here I thought it was something that actually mattered.

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: You're naive, you know? I gave up on that hokum long ago.

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: What, you don't want them to start treating us better?

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: You think the lords actually care about us Infected? On your bike!

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: I guarantee you, this bill thing's bound to fail. It'll be unanimous, even. And then it'll be like nothing ever happened.

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: They're doing this just for show, I tell you.

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: Aha! Too bad, then! You're wrong.

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: The bill didn't pass, but it didn't fail either.

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: It was a tie. The final decision's going to have to wait till next time.

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: I'm still not buying it. It won't pass. What does the paper say, though? What's in that bill, specifically?

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: One second. Let's see... I remember some bits and pieces of it back when they announced it.

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: Oh, take a look. It says here that Infected workers cannot work more than fifteen hours a day, that the factories have to give the Infected the same kinds of Originium protective equipment as non-Infected...

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: Pfft. Don't make me laugh.

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: There's a snowball's chance that's true. What's that saying again? There's no pies in the sky?

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: What would you outlanders even know? Me, I'm a born-and-bred Caladonian. I've seen how they do things my whole life. No one knows the nobles how I do.

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: You're still counting on those stingy tosspots to do anything for you out of their pockets? Dream on.

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: *Sigh*... You want to at least hold out some hope... Keep a positive outlook on things.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: There's no need to be so negative. Who could've thought ten years ago that they'd pass that New Caladonian Infected Act, right?

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: Now that, that's apples to oranges.

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: Us Infected can work their factories, and the heads only have to pay us half the money. They get to pocket the other half! Of course they passed that bill!

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: That's true. Oftentimes, they don't even pay us with cash, just Wage Tickets.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: Things take time. I think you could be more optimistic about this.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: Keep in mind that Caladon willingly accepts Infected from all the cities out there, and even offers work. You don't see that anywhere else in Victoria.

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: I heard from some of the foremen these policies are... what... 'Columbian-style?'

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: Are all the Columbian cities like this?

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: Well... It's complicated. There's a tiny bit of difference.

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: Whatever, time for a new topic. Any other news?

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: Let's see...

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: 'Terror in Caladon! Loud Roars Heard Underground at Night!'

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: And then... 'Possible Infected Smuggling Activity Spotted in Abandoned Districts in Caladon Outskirts.'

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: Then there's also this... 'Public Safety in Jeopardy, Convicts and Wanted Criminals Have Infiltrated the Infected Community.'

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Why are all the headlines like that?

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: That's the 'Caladon Daily' and their rubbish reporting for you. They love their terrorizing headlines, and they take care to add the word 'Infected' in there. Just talking about those hack journos makes me want to puke.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: It's true, but you should still be careful, Susie. Caladon hasn't been all that safe lately.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Hahaha... I'll watch out. Thanks.
November 17th, 1097, 8:40 A.M.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Fin fillets, potatoes, green onions... I guess that's about it?

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Oh, and the pepper, too!

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: I just have to deliver these to Mr. Kells, right?

steps.name: Citizen
steps.text: Yes, please.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: On my way!

steps.name: Protester
steps.text: Foreigners go home!

steps.name: Protester
steps.text: Out with the Infected! This is our home!!

steps.name: Loud-Mouthed Man
steps.text: Out with the Infected!

steps.name: Loud-Mouthed Man
steps.text: It's the Infected's fault us porters lost all our jobs!
It's not uncommon to find people protesting the Infected community here in Caladon.
When the city council passed the New Caladonian Infected Act four years ago, a large group of Infected migrated to the city for work all at once.
But the hostility between the non-Infected and the Infected didn't improve.

steps.name: Loud-Mouthed Man
steps.text: Hey, you! The Infected there! Get over here!

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: I-I'm just walking past...

steps.name: Loud-Mouthed Man
steps.text: What's that you're holding? Eh?

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: It's just...

steps.name: Loud-Mouthed Man
steps.text: What's that in your basket! Let me see it!

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: These are items I'm delivering to a customer!

steps.name: Loud-Mouthed Man
steps.text: Shouldn't your lot be working in the factories right now? What are you wandering around here for?!

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: It's part of my job to deliver things too...

steps.name: Loud-Mouthed Man
steps.text: Who said you could talk back?!

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Urgh...

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: (Ouch...)

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Spark... Arts...

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: (Bear with it, Susie... Don't fight back...)

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: (This isn't the first time something like this has happened...)

steps.name: Loud-Mouthed Man
steps.text: What gives you Infected the right to walk the streets in broad daylight anyway?

steps.name: Loud-Mouthed Man
steps.text: It's all your fault the air here has gotten so polluted!

steps.name: Loud-Mouthed Man
steps.text: Bunch of pests! Go back to the sewers, where you belong!

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: (But you're the one who came to the Infected community...)

steps.name: Loud-Mouthed Man
steps.text: What? What are you looking at me for? Looking for a fight?!

steps.name: Red
steps.text: That's enough, mister. Let's not overdo it.

steps.name: Loud-Mouthed Man
steps.text: And who are you?
The tall, masked man helps the Feline girl up and turns around to face the thug.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: There's no reason to lay hands on an unarmed lady now. It's not a very honorable thing to do, wouldn't you agree?

steps.name: Loud-Mouthed Man
steps.text: What? She's just an Infected!

steps.name: Loud-Mouthed Man
steps.text: And what's with you? Trying to be a hero?

steps.name: Loud-Mouthed Man
steps.text: Well? If you want some, come and get it!

steps.name: Loud-Mouthed Man
steps.text: Coward.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Mr. Red!

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: I'm afraid I don't have what it takes to offend you, kind sir.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Though before you continue, I should inform you that I have Originium crystals on my face, and your punch landed right on one.

steps.name: Loud-Mouthed Man
steps.text: W-What...?

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Oh, sir, this isn't good. Look, I'm bleeding out of my mouth, and your hand is injured.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: It might just get you infected too.

steps.name: Loud-Mouthed Man
steps.text: What?! But...!

steps.name: Protester
steps.text: Hurry! To the hospital! You can still make it!

steps.name: Loud-Mouthed Man
steps.text: Damn you, Ursus! You'd better watch your back! You'll regret this!

steps.name: Protester
steps.text: Enough now! Get to the hospital!

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Um, thanks... Mr. Red.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: A-Are you okay?

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Don't worry about me. I'm used to taking a beating.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: I could ask you the same. Look at your face. It's all swollen.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: I-I'm okay... I'll put some ice on it when I get home.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: There've been more anti-Infected protests here lately. You should avoid this area on your way back.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Where are you headed? I'll go with you.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Thanks, but don't you have work? I wouldn't want to be a bother...

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Don't worry yourself. I have errands in the area too.
Mr. Red works at a nearby factory, and he visits the shop sometimes.
He may be from Ursus, but he doesn't like to drink. He prefers to read a book in the shop all by himself.
The other workers seem to really respect him. They all call him 'the bossman'.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: But... Mr. Red, is that man really going to catch Oripathy?

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Of course not. You don't just get infected like that. I was only scaring him.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Oripathy can spread through blood, but he only had some minor scrapes.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: It's pretty effective as a bluff, though.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Hahaha, I see.

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: Those bastards... What a lot of utter scumbags!

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: Laying hands on a young lady? Have they no shame?

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Don't get yourself all worked up. I'm okay.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: So they ran off after they hit you? Did you see where they went?

steps.name: Red
steps.text: They ran north, so my guess is they headed to the Boil.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: The Boil, eh? It won't be easy to find them, then.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: In any case, I'll make a note. They've been fairly short staffed at the Guards lately.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Does your face still hurt? Need me to massage it a bit?

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Haha... It's okay. Don't worry about me, Officer Grani.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: It's true how Caladon hasn't been that safe lately... but I didn't expect you to get attacked, Susie.
Officer Grani isn't with the local Caladon Guards. She's a Mounted Police officer temporarily loaned to the local guards and assigned to the Infected community.
Of course, the Caladon Guards aren't very interested in keeping the Infected safe. This 'short staffed' business seems to be an excuse, too.
Which makes Officer Grani one of very few local law enforcement officers willing to help the Infected.
Though just the few of them alone... can't solve all of the community's safety problems.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: No loss of property... and that's filed. This is all I can do for you right now.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: I'm off now. Come find me if there's any more trouble.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Thank you, Officer Grani.

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: The idiots better hope I don't find them first.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: What if you do find them?

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: I'll beat the life out of them!

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Think, Stone. The moment you lay a finger, everyone around will start screaming and making a fuss.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Then, the next morning, the front page of 'Caladon Daily' will read 'Infected Batters Innocent Citizen, Security Problems Worse by the Day.'

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: Well...

steps.name: Red
steps.text: And I remember that rotten boy and his loud mouth.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: A month ago, he was protesting the crowd in overalls, complaining how the factory he worked at was shut down because of the Infected.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Two months ago, he protested with the hawkers and said the Infected stole his merchandise.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: So what is he today?

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: I think he said he was a 'porter'?

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: What in the world!

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: Sounds like something the gangs of the Boil would do. He was probably hired. Now which lord did we offend again?

steps.name: Red
steps.text: The Infected community's always been a thorn in the side of certain people. As long as the councilors who support the new bill aren't in the majority, these things will keep happening.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: We'd better keep our eyes peeled.

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: This prick, though... Forget Susie. He even tried to fight you, bossman, and how dare he!

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Alright, enough. Your pint's getting lonely.

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: *Sigh*... How am I supposed to drink, knowing our little Sparky got harassed?

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Hahaha, you're just exaggerating.

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: Sparky, take this.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Huh? What is it?

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: It's an ointment that helps reduce swelling. Anywhere it hurts, just rub some on there after you wash your face tonight.

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: Huh? Now how come you're not giving me some of that?

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: This is from Yan! You know how expensive it is? Besides, look how rough you are! What do you need it for?!

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Oh... If it's that expensive, I can't take it.

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: No, do. Best not work a pub with a swollen face.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Hahaha... This isn't exactly a pub, though...

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Thanks, Mr. Bean.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: In that case, your drinks are on the house tonight.

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: Now that's what I'm talking about!

steps.name: Exhausted Woman
steps.text: Susie, are you sure you have to go?

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Yes, Mum... Staying here... isn't going to do any of us any good.

steps.name: Exhausted Woman
steps.text: No, Susie, listen to me... I found another job this month. Don't worry about the medicine. We'll figure something out!

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Please don't... I can't be a burden on the family anymore, not when my baby brother and sister still have school. And when my big brothers are all still healthy.

steps.name: Exhausted Woman
steps.text: I can't let my daughter go to another city alone!

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Don't worry about me. I heard how the Infected working in Caladon get medicine as part of their pay.

steps.name: Exhausted Woman
steps.text: I'm sorry... It's all my fault, Susie... I'm so sorry.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: I'll take care of myself. Don't worry, Mum.
November 18th, 1097, 9:20 A.M.
Every now and then, I dream of my family.
I was born in Boschendal, a small town at the northern edge of Victoria.
When I was little, back when my father was still alive, he would take our whole family out to picnics.
When you're up on Mount Shay, gazing out into the distance, you can even see the vast Kazimierzian Plains.
It's been five years since the last time I went home, but my mother still sends me letters.
My family's situation has taken a turn for the better since I left. It was difficult to pay all the expenses an Infected needs with just my mother and my brothers' income.
They're living a better life, and that's more than enough for me.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Welcome!

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Look who's here!

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Huh? Hi, boss!

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Li'l~ Susie~

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Let me give your ears a good rub!

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Hahaha... boss... that tickles!

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Boss again? Come on, don't be such a stranger!

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Hahaha... Miss Quercus.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Quercus...

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: That's more like it!
Quercus is a free-spirit, and also the owner of the shop.
Although most people here treat it like a pub, it's actually Quercus's arboretum and lighting shop.
Many have asked us why she would open such a shop in the Infected community.
And her answer has always been a very simple one.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Why open a lighting shop?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Because I want to.
That said, Quercus actually spends very little time in Caladon.

The shop seems only to be a hobby of hers. In other words, she really meant it when she said she wanted to. She mostly works as a Messenger, spending her time bustling about in the wilderness. Most people call her the 'Druid of Gododdin.'
By the way, Quercus's Arts are actually very unique. She plants all kinds of strange flora around the shop, and she brewed most of the alcohol we sell here herself.
She even gave me my staff and Arts Unit because they can apparently help me control my own Originium Arts.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Why did you come back this time? Did you need something?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Oh? I'm not allowed to come see you without a special reason?

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Hahaha...

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: I have something to take care. What, have you forgotten? It's almost the end of the year!

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Oh, right...
This is a defining moment for me.
I've been saving up money for a few years now. I want to buy this place.
I want to have my own shop here in Caladon. No matter what I do, this will be the beginning of my independence.
And Quercus often tells me that the shop's landlord has been thinking about renting to someone else, and that she doesn't have much time to take care of it.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: So you've saved up all this? That's amazing, Susie!

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: But, Quercus... Are you sure it's okay? Isn't it a bit on the low side for a place like this?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: How many times have you asked me that now? Do you not trust me?

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: No, I mean... Of course I trust you.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: I'll get you a meeting with the landlord sometime next week for you to work out the details. He's a dependable one.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Next week, huh...?
November 18th, 1097, 9:56 P.M.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Here's your tea, Miss Mountbelan.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Thanks.
Ethelflaed Julie Mountbelan is one of our regulars. She's just Miss Mountbelan to us.
She's another of Rhodes Island's experts. She's in charge of coming up with solutions to solve Infected problems for the council.
Just like Mr. Root, she got along with our other customers straight away.
The Mountbelan name is known far and wide in the country, so I still haven't grown completely used to seeing a lady from such a prestigious family having tea around the Infected community.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Judging by your look, I suppose the lords did something to make you unhappy?
Miss Mountbelan takes a sip of tea. Both her lips and the blood vessels on her forehead are twitching.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Can you believe it? Can you believe it?!

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: I spent two weeks preparing all that data, and they only read a single page of it!

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Just one page!!

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: How short-sighted can they be?! The issues I raised are urgent to the point they need addressing right now! You can't tell me it doesn't worry them one bit?!

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Oh, they don't worry about the fire until it's started burning them.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: It this drags on, it'll immolate them completely.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Hasn't the Reunion mayhem in Gododdin taught them anything?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: The flames of Reunion Gododdin were stomped out two years ago. Why would it be a problem to these noble lords?

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Things aren't that simple, though! It's as though they don't even understand the crux of the matter! Reunion isn't just a band of thugs or bandits. There's a reason they started that uprising.

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: Oi, is it just me or did it get warmer in here all of a sudden?

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: Yeah, I think it did.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Not again. Cool it a little. Don't burn my store down.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: *Sigh*... Never mind.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Hahaha... Calm down, Miss Mountbelan.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: You're off work. Try to keep a happier face on, I think.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Here, give these a try.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: What do you have here... Sweets?

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: That's right. Quercus made these vanilla mints herself. Let them calm your rage.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: *Sigh*... Thanks...

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: I was on a holiday in Siesta just a few months ago... and now I'm starting to miss that place.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: It sounds like you've really had it tough, Miss Mountbelan. Loosen up some if you can.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: At least I have you lot to listen to me grumble here.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: You can't do that at Rhodes Island?

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: You think my case is bad? Everyone has it tough there... Kicking up a fuss at work would only hurt morale.

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: Don't worry, we're all a bunch of idiots. By the time you finish a sentence, we've gone and forgotten what you said.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: So, what conclusion did the lords arrive at?

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Well, halfway through the meeting, they started fixating on all those silly rumors.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: You mean like the 'sounds in the city underground' and 'criminals have infiltrated the Infected community?'

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: In the end, it's all the Infected's fault, eh?

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Right, it's all just baseless conspiracy theories. It's a mystery to me who's even been spreading them.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Anyway, the meeting devolved into a pointless shouting match after that.

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: It sounds like a lot of the lords support the Infected community, though?

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: We do solve a lot of their problems, after all. Some of the lords have made a good bit of dough over the last few years. Likelihood is they're just more amenable to it than most, considering they're directly profiting.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Besides, the community doesn't only concern the Infected anymore. There's plenty of non-Infected working here now, right?

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: That's true. I'm one of them right here.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Right, that's a fair point... but talking about it all here and now won't change a thing. I still have other engagements tomorrow, so if you'll excuse me.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Be careful out there.

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: Now setting that aside...

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: Why are you working here in our community, James? It's strange for me to say, but isn't it a bit risky, on shift with the Infected?

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: Risky... eh?

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: Tell you the truth, risks are, in the end, nothing more than an unknown. Putting food on the table, that's the immediate problem.

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: If worse comes to worst, suppose I actually catch Oripathy, my family are still going to live better than if I didn't have a job.

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: I've got two little mouths to feed. I can't just leave it to my wife to be the breadwinner. Besides, it's not like she makes much, selling scarves. We wouldn't be able to get by.

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: My mum's got asthma. It costs an arm and a leg to treat. My dad's got some serious bone disease too. He can't even get out of bed.

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: I don't have a choice. If only I could find better work...

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: *Sigh*... How come it sounds like your life's more of a mess than mine?

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: Why're you so quiet today, Stone? Did something happen?

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: *cough*... How old did James say his kids are again?

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: One's eight, the other twelve. Why?

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: No... No reason. Just thinking.

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: Come on, if you've got something on your mind, just say it. It's not like we're strangers.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Did you run into some kind of trouble, Stone?

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: Trouble, huh...? *Sigh*.

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: I-I got a letter from my wife. She said she'll come pay me a visit with our daughter.

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: A daughter? You have a daughter?!

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Eh? I didn't know you were married!

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: What?! Is it that strange to you?

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: No, not like that. Just... an Infected having a kid...

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: Oh, don't you worry about that. I caught Oripathy afterwards. My wife and daughter are fine.

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: Isn't that a good thing? Why the long face?

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: Right, you got Oripathy, and your wife didn't abandon you. Wish the missus cared about me like that.

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: *Sigh*, look at me. How am I supposed to face them the way I am now?

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: What's wrong with the way you are?

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: Right, why look down on yourself like that?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: It's true, though. You're not exactly in good shape to see her.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Why don't we get you a haircut? You could at least be a little better groomed?

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Alright! If it's a haircut Stone needs...

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: (Brandishes a pair of scissors and a comb)

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: Hold your beasties! You know how to cut hair, Sparky?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Now, don't underestimate her! My girl Susie's a master hairdresser.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Ta-dah!

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Well, doesn't that look pretty good?

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: I don't usually cut it so short. Feels all breezy...

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: Hey, you're looking fresh.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: I think you can do a lot for yourself if you pay just a little more attention to your hair, Stone.

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: *Sigh*. Look at me, though. My life's a disaster. How am I supposed to find time to care about my hair?

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Don't think like that!

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: It's because life's so hard that we should find our own ways to live better.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Right. No one's ever said the Infected have to live in misery.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Chin up. Your wife will be delighted to see you like this.

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: Take it slow. You come to my room later.

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: I've got some clean clothes I've been holding onto. Haven't worn them much. Give them a wash and see if they fit.

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: Eh... You sure about that?

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: What's to stand on ceremony? Just take them!

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: Now come on, drink up!
November 23rd, 1097, 10:35 A.M.
Today's the day.
I'm meeting the landlord.
There's a thick stack of cash in front of me.
Six thousand, five hundred pounds. This amount of money was once unthinkable to me.
When I was little, one of my brothers broke an Originium lamp we had. Mum gave him a really good spanking.
That was the first time I saw her get that angry. She needed that lamp to patrol the mineshaft at night.
The lamp was worth a hundred and fifty pounds. It was almost her entire month's salary. That's what got her so angry.
How many Originium lamps could six thousand and five hundred pounds buy?
I assess the enormity of the heavy, foul-smelling pile of sacrifice before me.
All the meals I've skipped over the years. All the hardships I've suffered through.
Six thousand, five hundred pounds.
These sheets of paper are like a bridge I laid myself, brick by brick. On the other side stands my dreams.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Susie! Get it together!

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: You're just meeting with the landlord! He's just a landlord!

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: From tomorrow onwards, you'll be the shop's owner! Your dream is coming true!

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: You're almost there, Susie!
I look in the mirror and give my cheeks a good slap.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: How should I greet him?

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: 'Nice to meet you, sir! I'm very glad to...'

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: No, the smile's too stiff.
My dream is about to come true, but I don't feel the least bit excited. On the contrary, I'm growing more and more afraid of seeing the man about to walk into the shop.
The landlord... What kind of a person is he?
Is he infected or not? Will he really sell the shop to me?
He's selling it to me so cheap. Could it be a scam?
Is he doing this because, like everyone else, he just wants to make fun of me, to humiliate me?
M-Maybe Quercus isn't Infected either... Maybe they're in on this together, just to...

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Ahhh! What am I thinking!
I smack my face hard.
I'm using pain to suppress these shameful, despicable emotions.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Don't be like this, Susie! This is hideous!
I stare into the mirror. The only thing that can be heard inside the quiet shop is the clock's ticking.
It's like torture.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Susie! Are you there?

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Ehhh?!

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Watch your Arts!

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: What's the matter with you? What are you so scared of? Did something happen?

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: No... I'm okay! Good morning, Miss Quercus.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: (Doubtful glare)

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Look at those dark circles under your eyes!

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: What's wrong? Did you not sleep well?

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Hahaha... I was a little nervous.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: Good morning, Miss Susie.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Oh! Mr. Root! Sorry, I didn't see...

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Huh? What time is it?

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Oh, sorry, Mr. Root. We aren't open today. Did you need something?

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: You haven't told her yet, Quercus?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Oh, you're right. I haven't.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: I forgot to mention it, but he's the landlord who owns the shop.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Eh?

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Ehhh??

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Mr. Root's the landlord? So the previous owners signed their contracts with Mr. Root?!

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: It's a long story... Anyway, Rhodes Island actually owns this property.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: I've heard the details from Quercus. Miss Susie, you want to buy the store, is that right?

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: Permit me to ask, then. What kind of business do you want to run here?

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Business?

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Oh! Business!

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: M-My father was a hairdresser.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: When I was little, he often said... we shouldn't change our attitude towards life just because we're poor.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Hairdressing may seem trivial, but if someone's putting in the effort to keep themselves groomed, then they must still carry the will to live.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: That's why I thought...

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: It would be nice... to open a hair salon in the Infected community.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: Hairdressing, huh...? For the Infected?

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: That sounds very nice.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: It's a deal, then! Someone will come to sort out the contract later.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Eh? That's it?

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: We've known each other for a long time, haven't we? You'll be fine, Susie.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: My own shop... It feels like... I'm dreaming.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: That reminds me. Where will you go now, Miss Quercus? Are you going to leave the city?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Oh, don't look at me like that. It's not like I won't ever come back.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: I'll stop by every now and then. I have lots of friends in town, you know?

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: Oh, and one last thing.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: Susie, Quercus got you a little gift.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: A gift? Huh?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Come, Susie. Everyone's waiting for you.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Congratulations!

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: You did it, Susie!

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Officer Grani! Why are you here?!

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: Alright! Now Sparky's the owner! Make sure you keep the booze we like on the taps!

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Congratulations, Susie.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Mr. Red! Aren't you supposed to be working?!

steps.name: Stone the Infected
steps.text: Oh, we took the day off. We weren't going to miss the moment you took over the shop.

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: That's right. I've been coming here every day for the last few years now. I probably know this place better than I do my own home.

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: Your wife could give you a good socking for that.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Alrighty, then. Miss Susie, our new owner, the shop is all yours!

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Oh, why are you tearing up? Don't cry!

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: Yeah, no crying.

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: Life's been hard for all of us lately. It's not often we get something to celebrate, yeah?

steps.name: James the Worker
steps.text: Cheer up!

steps.name: Bean the Infected
steps.text: Anyway, it doesn't matter what you turn the place into. I'll be here.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Hahaha... What's this? Tears of joy?

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: (Breaking up) Miss Quercus... I...

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Okay, okay now. No more tears...
My dream—
To the Infected, dreams are distant and unattainable.
My dream has always been to have my own shop, my own life.
So I wouldn't have to be a burden on my family anymore.
And now, my dream is about to come true. It's an unimaginable luxury for an Infected.
Does that make me lucky?
November 24th, 1097, 6:35 A.M.
Smoke...
A thick layer of smoke spreads from a corner of the Infected community, breaking the morning tranquility.

steps.name: Guards Member
steps.text: Evacuate the nearby residents first!

steps.name: Guards Member
steps.text: You there, quit dawdling about! Nothing to see here!

steps.name: Firefighter
steps.text: Over here! The fire's still going!

steps.name: Firefighter
steps.text: Check again for casualties! This is the Infected community!

steps.name: Firefighter
steps.text: Look for any traces of Originium, like damaged appliances!

steps.name: Firefighter
steps.text: Don't let any activated dust spread!

steps.name: Guards Member
steps.text: Bloody hell... Why's somebody setting fires around here?!

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Why...

steps.name: Guards Member
steps.text: Evacuate everyone first! Hey, you, Feline over there! What are you doing?!
Smoke...
The smoke and scorched stench fill the air.
The burning leather and timber crack apart in the lingering heat.

steps.name: Firefighter
steps.text: Don't run in there! Are you daft?!

steps.name: Guards Member
steps.text: Hold her back!

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Why...
The girl is unwilling to believe what she sees before her. She wants to close her eyes.
This has to be a dream.
This has to be a bad dream.
Right. The moment she opens her eyes, she'll be free of this nightmare.
Yes, when she open her eyes, she'll be greeted by the same old ceiling. A new day awaits her. A new day with her own shop.
But the shop before her is nothing but a pile of rubble engulfed in flames.
Of the sign that once read 'Green Spark,' nothing remains but a few burnt fragments. It matches the walls and ceiling, long since rendered ash.
Before her eyes lies what was once her dreams, her hopes, and her future.
All of it now buried in this burning rubble.

steps.name: Susie
steps.text: Why...?
The will that once helped the Feline girl through countless tribulations can support her small body no longer.
She falls to her knees.
The scorching ashes burns her hands and legs. The broken fragments cut through her skin.

a.text: In the ruins of despair, an Infected lost everything.
And so the blaze is extinguished.
